newsitem.title: USA: Swaps new business up 20.2 pct first half-ISDA.
newsitem.headline: Swaps new business up 20.2 pct first half-ISDA.

text.p: New business activity in swaps and other privately negotiated derivatives increased 20.2 percent in the first half of 1996, according to the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA).

Global new business in interest rate swaps, currency swaps and interest rate options amounted to $8.310 trillion in notional principal in the first half of 1996, compared with $6.911 trillion in the six months ended December 31, 1995, ISDA said.

More specifically, activity in interest rate swaps rose 23.7 percent in the first six months of 1996 to $6.520 trillion, currency swaps gained 24.1 percent to $374.03 billion, and interest rate options (caps, collars, floors and swaptions) gained 5.7 percent to $1.416 trillion.

In addition, transactions in all categories that were outstanding -- contracts yet to reach maturity or otherwise terminate -- totaled $21.069 trillion notional compared with $17.712 trillion at the end of 1995. That represented an increase of 19.0 percent.

The notional amount of outstanding interest rate swaps rose 21.6 percent to $15.584 trillion. Currency swaps outstanding rose 8.2 percent to $1.295 trillion and outstanding interest rate options rose 13.1 percent to $4.190 trillion, ISDA said.
